title: BTS Star RM Shares His Art Collection, and Fans Flock to the Museum
summary:
RM, the leader of the K-pop band BTS, is showing art from his own collection at a museum for the first time. The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, called SFMOMA, has been packed with fans eager to see it.

The show is called "RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me." It has more than 170 works, mostly from RM's collection, with a few pieces from the museum, such as a painting by Mark Rothko shown next to one by Korean artist Yun Hyong-keun. The museum's gift shop said it stocked more souvenirs than for any exhibition before.

RM, whose real name is Kim Nam-joon, is 32. He began visiting museums and collecting art nearly a decade ago. Art has inspired some of his songs. His collection focuses on Korean artists from ancient times to today. BTS fans, known as ARMY, even made up a word, "Namjooning," for doing the things he loves, like visiting museums.

RM said he asked two questions when choosing art: Does it really move him, and does it still have something to say to people today? He called the show "a pretty long introduction" to himself.

Fans Bre Walker and Joi Karra visited on the first preview day. Walker said it was her first time ever in an art museum. In one section, they spotted seven carved wooden ducks and wondered if it was a nod to the seven members of BTS. A rock carved with the word "candy" left them puzzled, which seemed fitting in a section called "I don't know … but I like it."

Fans also shared handmade gifts. One visitor flew in from Zambia. After her visit, Walker said, "I'll be back."
why_it_matters: A pop star's love of art is bringing many young fans into a museum for the first time, showing how music and art can inspire each other.
